newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Sulzer Medica eyes acquisitions soon.
newsitem.headline: Sulzer Medica eyes acquisitions soon.

text.p: Stock market newcomer Sulzer Medica will not wait much longer to make acquisitions in its core business of orthopaedics and cardiovascular equipment, chief executive Andre Buchel told a Swiss newspaper.
Buchel told the business bi-weekly Finanz und Wirtschaft the company kept a wishlist of acquisition targets.
It could mobilise around one billion Swiss francs for this purpose after starting trading on the Swiss stock exchange and as American Depositary Shares (ADS) in New York.
"But now we will not wait much longer, without rushing into anything," he told the newspaper.
"The acquisition plans involve both our main areas of business," Buchel told Finanz und Wirtschaft.
"In orthopaedics, we want to move forward in the trauma area -- bone treatment due to accidents -- and sport medicine and offer products for the human backbone.
"In the cardiovascular area, we are aiming for biotechnology applications," he added.

Sulzer Medica posted sales of 1.16 billion Swiss francs in 1996 and employed 4,557 people. It designs, manufactures and markets a range of implantable orthopaedic and cardiovascular products such as hip joints and heart valves.
The group started trading on the stock markets on Monday after being spun off by parent Sulzer AG, which retains three-quarters of Sulzer Medica equity.

Sulzer launched the public offering to generate cash for Sulzer Medica's expansion through research, development and acquisition without draining much-needed funds from Sulzer's diverse engineering and machinery divisions.
Asked how big Sulzer Medica's warchest was for buying new businesses, Buchel said:
"Our own cash-flow, other outside capital and approximately 800 million Swiss francs ($543.5 million) from going public allow us to utilise more than one billion Swiss francs."
"With this we can also set our sights on buying bigger companies," he said without elaborating on potential targets.
